Q: my UI functions randomly stopped working when I created a new project A:

You need to put the calls inside the Scaffold. That's why the Greeting shows up- it's inside the Scaffold. The Scaffold takes the entire screen.

Q: MS Access re-uses already established ODBC connections, disregarding differing connection parameters A:

This is expected behaviour. Access caches the connection after the first successful connection to the same database.

Apart from that, it doesn't make much sense to attempt to open several connections to the same database.

More on this: Access Caching ODBC connection settings.

Q: Problems formatting Rust code in presence of dioxus `rsx!` macro A:

Yes, that's the norm. rustfmt can't parse the rsx! macro's custom syntax, and when it hits one it often bails out on the entire block, leaving surrounding code - like the handle_poker_message call and its arguments - misformatted.

Dioxus ships its own formatter, dx fmt, specifically for RSX. To make your editor use it, tell rust-analyzer to call dx fmt instead of rustfmt. In Emacs with lsp-mode, add this to .dir-locals.el:

((rust-mode . ((lsp-rust-analyzer-rustfmt-override-command . ["dx", "fmt"]))))

After that, saving will format with dx fmt.

Be aware that dx fmt and rustfmt sometimes disagree on whitespace (issue), so you may need to run dx fmt then cargo fmt to pass CI. Also, the --all-code flag has been known to occasionally break async closures, so sticking to the plain dx fmt is safer.

Q: Catching problem of multiple (non-equivalent) type definitions with the same name in C A:

If you have multiple implementation files that define the structure individually, there is no mechanism in the widely spread compiler systems that prevent the situation you describe. (Disclaimer: at least to my knowledge.)

At the end of the day, this is more a question of software architecture than tooling. Each programming language has its flaws, and C is full of such. Each project should have a code style guide, a software architecture, a code review process, and so on to prevent errors induced by undisciplined, unconscious, and other "random" development.

One common solution is to provide the structure definition in a separate header file, for example with a specific name or a "private" prefix or suffix. All sources needing the structure definition include this additionally, instead of trying to reinvent the wheel.

My personal experiences with code quality checking tools are limited, because I'm used to work in professional environments, providing said abstract documents. However, there are static C code analyzers out there that can find such implementation errors over all sources of an application. Please use your web search Fu for them. This Wikipedia page might be a good start for your research

Q: How can I pause a 'repeating forever' animation in Reality Composer Pro 2? A:

RCP2 has no Pause action for a forever loop. You must control playback in code with AnimationPlaybackController.

Make sure supports pausing is on in the Animation Inspector, and in the behavior’s PlayAnimationAction, enable Use Parented Controllers (documentation). This sets useParentedControllers: true so the controller can be paused from code.

var playbackController: AnimationPlaybackController?

// Get the character entity
guard let scene = ARViewContainer.loadedEntity?.scene,
      let character = scene.findEntity(named: "YourCharacterName") else { return }

// Subscribe to playback events
scene.publisher(for: AnimationEvents.PlaybackStarted.self, on: character)
    .sink { event in
        playbackController = event.playbackController
    }
    .store(in: &cancellables)

Now call playbackController?.pause() / playbackController?.resume() when needed.

The controller remains valid while the animation loops, so you set it once.
